title: Before the Long Trip
logline: A fishing family spends the day before a multi-day trip securing the house, settling debts, and telling neighbours exactly when to expect the boat back, so that being unreachable for days does not mean being irresponsible.

object.note: Object 10 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Readiness for the sea becomes preparation for leaving it for a while: a fishing family settling everything before days out of reach.

thread_out.thread: Stepping away without abandoning anyone leads to a final giving away: an elderly woman emptying a house of sixty years, and a doorway that becomes Chathura's road toward the crowd.

requirements: A fishing family with a real multi-day trip during the filming window
Consent to film both departure preparations and, if possible, the return
No filming of the trip itself unless it can be done safely

lesson.in_simple_terms: Stepping away for a while can be done responsibly: you secure what you leave, tell people when you will be back, and keep that promise. The texts describe even their deepest withdrawal this way, with duties to others attached.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ටික කලකට ඈත් වීම වගකීමෙන් කළ හැකිය: ඉතිරි කර යන දේ ආරක්ෂා කර, ආපසු එන දිනය අන් අයට කියා, ඒ පොරොන්දුව රැකීමයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts describe the attainment of cessation (nirodha samāpatti): a period, resolved in advance, in which mind stops altogether while the body stays alive and warm, open only to non-returners and arahants who have mastered all eight attainments. Before entering, the practitioner performs four preliminary duties (pubbakicca): making sure belongings are protected, being ready to answer the community's call, being ready to answer the Teacher's summons, and checking how much life remains. The texts call it dwelling at ease in Nibbāna here and now, and like every deep state they describe, it depends on being able to enter and leave at a chosen time.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The day before departure the family secures the house and boat, settles accounts, and tells neighbours exactly when to expect the boat back and who to call. The film then waits with those left behind, watching the weather and the calendar until the return date. The viewer sees for themselves that being out of reach and being irresponsible are not the same thing.

key_terms.en: attainment of cessation: a resolved period in which mind and mental factors do not occur
the four preliminary duties before entering
dwelling in the happiness of nibbāna here and now

lesson.caution: The fishing trip is a secular parallel, not an equivalent: the texts' cessation is a rare attainment of people far along the path, not a nap, a digital detox or an escape from responsibility.
lesson.builds_on: The lifeguards' readiness faced the sea; this film prepares to leave it for a while, echoing the texts' insistence that even the deepest withdrawal keeps its obligations.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
